title: What Learning Board is made of
oneLine: A web app: React and TypeScript around the Excalidraw canvas, our smart ink and learning layer on top, saved in your browser and served by a small Node server.

nodes.label: Your browser
nodes.sub: Chrome or Edge, draws on the GPU

nodes.label: Excalidraw
nodes.sub: open-source canvas: shapes, arrows, zoom, undo

nodes.label: Google handwriting
nodes.sub: only for To text and hold C

nodes.label: Vite
nodes.sub: builds it into small, fast files

steps.say: You draw in your browser. The board is a canvas the graphics card paints, which is why it stays smooth.
The code is TypeScript with React for the screens. Vite builds it into small files; a tiny Node server (server.mjs) serves them on this computer.
The canvas itself is Excalidraw, an open-source drawing engine: shapes, arrows that stay attached, text, zoom and undo come from it.
Our smart ink watches every stroke. Pure geometry (no AI) decides in under a millisecond whether it was meant to be a circle, a box or a line, and hands back the perfect shape.
The learning layer is ours too: flowing dots on a see-through canvas, steps and Play, quiz cards, art styles, and the / blocks for arrays, trees and graphs.
Boards are saved in IndexedDB, a small database inside your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
Only one thing goes online: when you ask to turn writing into text, the pen strokes are sent to Google's handwriting reader.
A service worker keeps a copy of the app, so it installs like a program and opens even offline.
Lessons are plain JSON files. The Node server watches the folder and sends a new lesson to the open page within a second.
